title: The Mantis Shrimp Has 12 Color Receptors but Sees Color Worse Than You

scenes.text: The strangest eyes in nature see colors worse than yours.
A mantis shrimp's eyes have up to 16 kinds of photoreceptors. You have four.
Twelve of them detect color. You have three.
So scientists expected superhuman color vision.
The test shocked them. The shrimp couldn't tell colors 15 nanometers apart. People spot one or two.
Twelve color receptors, and a worse eye for shades.

description:
The strangest eyes in nature see colors worse than yours.
Mantis shrimp can have up to 16 types of photoreceptors, 12 tuned to color, yet tests found they fail to tell apart colors that people can easily separate. Scientists think the shrimp uses a simpler way to process color.
What would you want to see with mantis shrimp eyes? Comment below.
